newsitem.title: FRANCE: Male AIDS suffers said getting best care in France.
newsitem.headline: Male AIDS suffers said getting best care in France.

text.p: Male AIDS sufferers get the best treatment for the disease in France, an AIDS awareness group said on Friday in a report urging more help for women and drug addicts.
The review of 604 patients by the group AIDES said 32 percent of drug users and 26 percent of women with the disease had no regular medical surveillance, against just 6.5 percent of male sufferers.
"Today in France it's better to be a man who does not take drugs than a woman who uses drugs," Jerome Soletti, an AIDES leader, told a news conference.

Twenty-four percent of women in France, the European country hardest hit by AIDS, reckoned they were not properly informed about the disease against 16 percent of men. AIDES urged an end to "glaring inequalities".
Many female suffers in France were "foreigners more concerned with looking after their children," Soletti said.

Michel Destot, the Socialist mayor of Grenoble, told the news conference: "The current restrictive legislation forces drug addicts to live in semi-secrecy. It sets them apart from the healthcare system."
He urged a better balance between cracking down on drugs and helping AIDS sufferers. AIDES estimates that 150,000 to 200,000 people in France have AIDS.
